items.residual: B1 — SE share deletion / SE + old-owner collusion (T-SE-1). The irreducible statechain trust unit. [BATCH 1, item index 0 = known_residuals[0]]
items.the_bound: None, and the one structural limit offered is itself unobservable. The correct predicate is NOT 'received before the compromise' but 'received before RETENTION began' — and retention start is exactly the quantity A3 says cannot be verified from outside. WHICH coins is therefore unknown to the victim as well as unbounded in count.
items.exposure_if_open: Full value of every coin the SE co-signed for since retention began, spent in one fresh 2-of-2 signature via private relay, with no timelock, no trigger, and no mempool warning the defender can act on.
items.challenge: The bucket stands and the item's core kill is correct — PROTOCOL.md:649's '≥144 blocks of on-chain notice' is false for B1, because a fresh co-signature under A spends F directly and never broadcasts T. Three corrections. (1) The item under-collects the comfortable sentence: the same clause appears in SPEC-FOUNDATION §1's B1 row ('a public on-chain trigger plus ≥144 blocks of notice') and REQ-3's whole verdict is worded 'MET; unchanged in kind, IMPROVED IN NOTICE' on the strength of it. Delete one and it still stands in two places. (2) The item repeats the doc's other comfortable sentence in softer form. Its own bound says 'a coin received before the compromise and never touched since is safe', which is PROTOCOL:643's 'pre-hack coins left untouched are unconditionally safe' and G7. That holds only for a hack modelled as a point-in-time snapshot of current shares. B1's premise is RETENTION, which is longitudinal: if the SE retained shares from before the coin was received, the attacker holds SE_old for it and the colluding sender's retained sender_share completes A (sender_share + SE_old == A). 'Unconditionally safe' must become 'safe iff received after retention began', and since retention start is unobservable, that is not a safe set anyone can identify. (3) TRUST-MODEL:190 offers 'the current owner racing with a fee-bump wins in practice' as a mitigation; SPEC-FOUNDATION §1 gives the same adversary 'a fresh, no-timelock spend via PRIVATE RELAY', which is not raceable at all — and per item 6 the shipped presets carry fee_bump: None (config.rs:351,382), so the fee-bump the mitigation names does not exist in the default install. Two sentences in one corpus, opposite conclusions, and the code sides against the mitigation.

items.residual: B6 — Audit [17] residual, un-laddered lane only: the deposit-anchored deadline is late by k·interval for parents transferred k times pre-split. Claimed 'absorbed by the auto_exit margin (≥ k_max·interval + 144), not solved.' [BATCH 1, item index 5 = known_residuals[5]]
items.the_bound: Two rows, not one. LEAF / un-laddered: covered for k ≤ 14; uncovered lateness = (k − 14)·interval, worst admissible k = 99 (not 100) ⟹ 8,500 blocks ≈ 59 days, against a 2,120-block margin. WHOLE COIN, laddered or flat: no deadline is computed at all, so the margin is not late — it is never applied. The bound is on LATENESS; the loss it exposes is the whole coin.
items.exposure_if_open: Leaves: the holder loses the piece to the splitter's rung at L_0 − k·interval, up to ~59 days before auto_exit_due believes the deadline is. Whole received coins: nothing arms the predecessor's rung at L_{k-1} = own L_k + interval, so an idle received coin has no automatic action at all.
items.challenge: Bucket stands; the item's central correction (delete 'absorbed'; config.rs:248-258 calls 14 'the weakest term' in source and says only conveying ancestor locktimes can fix it) is verified. Two corrections. (1) OFF BY ONE THAT SHOWS THE NUMBER WAS COPIED: k = 100 is unreachable. At capacity L_k = H_dep, and lib/src/transfer/receiver.rs:665 refuses any backup with lock_time ≤ current_blockheight, so the deepest conveyable parent is k = 99 ⟹ (99−14)·100 = 8,500 blocks ≈ 59 days. (2) THE SCOPE IS THE REAL ERROR. 'Un-laddered lane only … a laddered coin has no absolute deadline to be late about' is the INV-27 reading that T-1 — a HIGH surviving flaw in this same document — retracts. On the whole-coin lane the coverage is not late, it is ABSENT: estimate_exit_cost returns exit_deadline_block = None whenever there are no branch rows (wallet.rs:3118), and auto_exit_due skips such coins at wallet.rs:1985 under the comment 'verified flat: no ancestor can race it'. That comment is false for every RECEIVED whole coin — the predecessor holds rung L_{k-1} = own L_k + interval, so the action deadline is one interval after the owner's own backup matures — and nothing arms it, since background_auto_refresh is false on both presets (config.rs:347,382). Published as 'un-laddered lane only', this row tells a reviewer the laddered lane is covered when it has zero coverage.

items.residual: SUB-ECONOMIC FINALITY — the sender's free option over a piece too small to defend; min_child_value = 1,310 is V_min at the hardcoded 2.0 sat/vB and correct at no other rate. [BATCH 1, item index 10 = known_residuals[10]]
items.the_bound: 'None' is too generous to the document. A bound is CONSTRUCTIBLE and is what the spec owes: V_min(d,r) is a closed form the tree already carries (SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY §1 reproduces PARTIAL-PAYMENT §6 to the sat), so the honest limitation is a published r*(V,d) table — r* = 2.01 for a floor-value piece, and a depth-1 10,000-sat piece under water between 5 and 10 sat/vB. What is genuinely unbounded is AGGREGATE exposure: nothing counts how many sub-economic pieces exist, and the marginal cost of voiding each further piece is zero.
items.exposure_if_open: Every payee holding a piece below V_min(d, r_live) loses it entire to the party who split it, at min(L_k) over the parent's flat backups, with no malice required. On the COLOURED lane the piece is not merely recovered by the sender — the allocation is DESTROYED and nobody acquires it.
items.challenge: Bucket stands and every figure I re-derived holds: min_child_value = (committed_fee(2.0)=250 + P2A 240)·2 + dust 330 = 1,310 (tesr.rs:158-165) with committed_fee_rate: 2.0 hardcoded in TesrParams::mainnet; BACKUP_TX_SIZE = 112; check_exit_headroom takes no value argument; a repo-wide grep for Viability/NotViable/SubEconomic over lib/ and clients/ returns nothing; fee_bump is None on both presets. Three challenges. (1) 'the_bound: None' is the wrong shape of honesty. Writing 'none exists' invites the reader to conclude the failure is unbounded when it is merely UNEVALUATED — the function exists, the inputs exist, nobody calls it. The named limitation should be the r* table plus the sentence 'admission is evaluated once, at claim, at a rate nobody knows (C-1)', not a blank. (2) THE COUPLING THE ITEM DROPS, and it is the half that discredits: RGB-2 establishes that every floor in the tree (min_child_value, colored_child_floor, colored_spine_tip_floor, V_min) is pure fee arithmetic with NO ASSET TERM, so a 1,310-sat carrier may hold an arbitrarily valuable allocation whose economic security is denominated in carrier sats. Pricing this row in sats only is the comfortable half. (3) owner_call = true is right for the ADMISSION decision (mint at 1,310, book at face value) but is being applied to the whole row. The receiver-side DISCLOSURE — surface the defence cost at the payee's own stress rate before claiming — is not a product judgement, it is owed work; folding it under owner_call is how it stays unbuilt.

items.residual: D17 — the Lightning latch clock is never bound to the HTLC's CLTV; unlock_by_preimage performs no expiry check; batch_id binding (C-8) absent. [BATCH 1, item index 15 = known_residuals[15]]
items.the_bound: None, and the missing clock is the smaller of two problems. Zero `cltv` hits across clients/, lib/ and server/ confirms the relation cannot be checked. But the gate that would enforce it lives inside the same operator trust domain as the party it constrains, so even a correct check would not make RECEIVE trustless.
items.exposure_if_open: In RECEIVE the USER is the payer (LIGHTNING.md §3 step 2) and the COORDINATOR mints the preimage (rand::thread_rng(), endpoints/lightning_latch.rs:79-89). The operator therefore holds the preimage from latch creation and can settle the user's held HTLC at any moment without ever delivering the coin. Separately, because a HODL invoice HOLDS the HTLC, the remaining CLTV at latch creation is the original delta MINUS the hold time, so the 3000 s latch can outlive the HTLC deadline with no exotic routing.
items.challenge: Bucket stands; the item's three-path account is exact (unlock_by_preimage at :215-282 reads no expiry; transfer_preimage at :134-152 and get_preimage's SQL at database/lightning_latch.rs:53-67 both gate and fail closed). But the item accepts the document's framing of WHAT RECEIVE RESTS ON, and that framing is the sentence a reviewer will use. Verified: the coordinator generates and stores the preimage in its own Postgres; SPEC-FOUNDATION §1 states the SSP 'is co-located with the coordinator and blind SE as ONE operator trust domain'; the user is the payer. So the expiry gate the item wants extended to the third path is the operator's own SQL constraining the operator's own LN node — it binds an honest operator's two arms and stops no adversary. LIGHTNING.md:75 ('the user cannot be robbed and the SSP cannot be robbed … RECEIVE needs no operator trust for safety'), :168 ('RECEIVE adds ZERO trust') and SPEC-FOUNDATION §1's 'Provably cannot rob the user in RECEIVE' are all false on that reading. LIGHTNING.md compounds it by attributing the mint to 'the SE' twice, which makes it read as an enclave property when the blind SE never sees the preimage. Second, the item's CLTV argument is stronger than it states: 3000 s looks safely inside any plausible cltv_expiry only if the latch starts when the HTLC arrives — but a HODL invoice exists precisely to hold, so the margin is original-delta minus hold-time and nothing measures either. The honest limitation is two sentences, not one: RECEIVE atomicity rests on (a) an SSP policy relating two clocks that the protocol never reads, and (b) the operator not settling early, which is the same trust bar as PAY.

items.residual: V10 / V11 — arithmetic residuals on attacker-reachable paths: Coin::amount is u32 so receive-path booking truncates above ~42.95 BTC; `let fee = tx0_output.value - total_output_value` runs before anything about the transaction is verified. [BATCH 1, item index 20 = known_residuals[20]]
items.the_bound: V11: real and correct — no signature is produced on any panicking path, so the loss is process availability. Add the surface: the abort reaches the BROWSER wallet (wasm/src/lib.rs:346) and the uniffi FFI, not only a Rust process. V10: the stated bound is false. 2^32 sat is a real ceiling, but 'zero sats move' is contradicted by the item's own exposure — the outcome is funds stranded in the 2-of-2.
items.exposure_if_open: V11: a crafted backup tx in a conveyed set aborts the receiver at claim or the SSP at pre-pay validation, in every build profile, remotely triggerable. V10: an oversized (or merely mismatched) funding is never booked as primary and never picked up as a duplicate, so no backup is ever co-signed and the funding is stranded — B5, i.e. value loss.
items.challenge: The bound is the problem. (1) 'ZERO SATS MOVE on any of these paths … the loss is availability of the validating process, not value' sits two paragraphs above the item's own 'the funds strand in the 2-of-2, a B5-class outcome'. That internal contradiction is exactly the sentence a reviewer quotes. I confirmed the stranding: the primary lane matches on `unspent.value == coin.amount.unwrap() as u64` (coin_status.rs:35-40), and check_for_duplicated only scans coins ALREADY IN_MEMPOOL/UNCONFIRMED/CONFIRMED (:213-215), so a funding that never matched the exact amount is never recovered by the duplicate lane either. Stranded funds are lost value. Note this is broader than 2^32: the exact-match selector strands ANY over-funding. (2) Credit where due, and it should be published: the ceiling guard the item calls unreachable at :50-57 IS reachable in the duplicate lane at :241-249, where it SKIPS rather than truncates — so the truncating casts that actually survive are the two receive-lane ones (receiver.rs:1263, transfer_receiver.rs:1619), and both UNDER-book (value mod 2^32 < value), which is the safe direction for a receiver and for a pre-paying SSP. That is the one genuinely bounded part of V10 and it is worth saying, because it is what stops the truncation from being an inflation attack. (3) V11's sharpening is confirmed and should replace the residual's text: the underflow at receiver.rs:595-596 wraps in release (no [profile.release] anywhere in the workspace) and only panics in debug, but witness.nth(0).unwrap() (:565), split_last().unwrap() (:568), Signature::from_slice().unwrap() (:570), tx0.output[vout] (:576) and XOnlyPublicKey::from_slice(spk[2..]).unwrap() (:578) abort in EVERY profile, and validate_backup_chain_v2:447 runs them per conveyed backup tx before any check succeeds.

items.residual: R-5 — Deep-DAG unilateral latency: 'depth-3 worst ≈ 60 days by the doc's model (the code's own model implies ≈30, and the three cost/latency models in the tree disagree — D6). Geometric per-level schedules would cap it at ~30 days ...; shipped as a dial, default off (O-4).' [BATCH 1, item index 25 = known_residuals[25]]
items.the_bound: Two ceilings, and publish the second. HONEST-SHAPE: depth-10 = 9,383 blocks ≈ 65.2 days (base 2,885 + 9·722), 23 transactions, against MAINNET_EPOCH 10,000. SHAPE-INDEPENDENT: check_exit_headroom requires Σ(csv+1) ≤ epoch_expiry_height − tip, and epoch_expiry_height = H_dep + initlock − k·interval with tip ≥ H_dep, so no admitted bundle of ANY shape can exceed initlock = 10,000 blocks ≈ 69.4 days. Depth-3 is 4,329 blocks ≈ 30.1 days.
items.exposure_if_open: Not open. A deeper tree is refused at claim; the latency can only be paid. But the ceiling SHRINKS with the parent's age and hop count (available = initlock − k·interval − age), so admissible depth falls toward 0 near the epoch boundary — that is T-4, and it belongs beside the number.
items.challenge: Bucket and bound stand — this is the one item where a genuinely enforced number exists and the DOCUMENT is what is wrong. Verified: exit_wait_blocks(base) = 2,885, per_level = 722, max_split_depth = 10, depth-10 chain = 9,383 blocks / 23 txs, SPINE_CSV = 0, and the gate is on the live claim path (verify_conveyed_child at tesr.rs:7479, reached from transfer_receiver.rs:765 and :1222). The doc contradiction is real: §5.9:426-427 calls the geometric schedule 'a shipped dial, default off' while §10 O-4 lists it as future work, and the only `geometric` hit in the tree is an unrelated batch-geometry comment at tesr.rs:2499 — no schedule code exists. Two additions. (1) THE ITEM UNDER-CLAIMS ITS OWN BOUND. Deriving 9,383 from the honest two-tier shape leaves it exposed to A8's open residual (cb.parent.params is a sender-declared serde field supplying the per-tier CSV bounds, so a sender declaring wide params relaxes its own bounds check). The epoch inequality is not: available ≤ initlock for any shape, forged or honest. Publish 10,000 blocks / 69.4 days as the hard ceiling and 9,383 / 65.2 days as the deepest honest child — a sender-proof bound is what makes this row survive review. (2) Keep the honest coupling and complete it. The 3× improvement is bought entirely by SPINE_CSV = 0, which collapses the payee's on-chain warning from ~4.07 years to ~15.7 days (PARTIAL-PAYMENT-ECONOMICS.md:575-576) — one decision, two consequences, and quoting 65.2 days without 15.7 days is the comfortable half.

items.residual: PROTOCOL.md §5.13's package-aware watch_pass (TES-fixable #4) is SPECIFIED BUT UNIMPLEMENTED for the default tower — 'the one place this document describes something that does not yet exist in code.' [BATCH 1, item index 30 = known_residuals[30]]
items.the_bound: The DEPLOYMENT condition is real and checkable (fee_bump: None on both presets; FeeBumpConfig at config.rs:313-328 requires core_rpc_url/user/password AND a hot fee-wallet secret key, so enabling it means running a Bitcoin Core node and a hot key, not flipping a flag). The EXPOSURE bound offered is false: there is no 112-vB fallback during a walk.
items.exposure_if_open: Full value of any coin whose tier is stuck above 2.0 sat/vB while F is already spent. Symmetric in the base case (the rival tier is also fixed-fee and pre-signed), asymmetric exactly to the extent a motivated attacker can hand-roll a P2A child while a default install cannot.
items.challenge: Re-bucket, because the stated bound fails in the only case that needs it. 'For a WHOLE coin this is bounded: the owner's own flat backup is the lowest rung, so their fallback is one 112-vB transaction at the spike rate' — the flat backups spend F, and so does T. A tier walk only happens AFTER T is broadcast, so by the time a tier is stuck the flat backup is permanently unconfirmable. This is the same fact T-1 states as 'the deadline is retired permanently the moment F is spent'. It holds whether the trigger was hostile or the owner's own. Second, even while F is unspent the backup is not an on-demand fallback: it carries an absolute locktime up to initlock blocks out. So the named fallback exists only in the scenario that never required a bump. What survives, and should replace it: (i) the keyless default watch_pass is not package-aware and by D31 never usefully could be (rescuing a 240-sat anchor was measured at ~900× its value); (ii) the owner path exists but ships off; (iii) turning it on is an infrastructure decision (Core RPC + hot fee key), not config; (iv) no test exercises spike-time bumping through the tower. And note the cross-item consequence the spec must not leave standing: B1's mitigation 'the current owner racing with a fee-bump wins in practice' (TRUST-MODEL:190) presumes precisely the capability that ships as None. owner_call stays true — shipping a rescue capability default-off and behind a Core RPC is a product decision about who is provisioned during a spike — but the row must be written as an open exposure with a deployment precondition, not as a bounded one.

items.residual: T-2 (surviving flaw) — the real on-chain maintenance cadence is set by the flat ladder, not the CSV hop budget; §7's footprint economics has no term for it. [BATCH 1, item index 35 = flaws[2]]
items.the_bound: A closed form per shape, all re-derived from the compiled-in mainnet params (10,000 / 100, 112-vB re-anchor, 144 blocks/day): idle received (k ≥ 1) → 69.44 d/epoch → ~589 vB/coin-yr; 1 tx/day → 40.98 d → ~998; 10 tx/day → 8.74 d → ~4,680; never-transferred (k = 0) → 0 vB/yr ONLY at the price of becoming exit-only after ~69 days.
items.exposure_if_open: No direct fund loss from the missing row itself — but the cadence is also UNPAID by default for the shape that owes it, and that half does end in loss (T-1/B6). §7.1's '0 vB/yr', §3's 'Idle on-chain footprint: 0', §7.2's ~320× and §8.2's C-90 rejection all rest on a denominator with a missing term.
items.challenge: Bucket stands; every figure re-derived and correct (flat_ladder_params('bitcoin') = (10_000, 100) at lib/src/tesr.rs:365 pinned at :796, mirrored in ci-guards' expected() table and docker-compose-main.yml:76-77; the item's note that VE-1's '50000' is wrong for this tree is confirmed). Two challenges, both in the direction of less comfort. (1) THE 'k = 0 → GENUINELY 0' ROW IS STILL ONE DEGREE TOO KIND, and it is the row §7.1 actually publishes. It is 0 only if the owner accepts that the coin becomes NON-TRANSFERABLE after initlock/144 ≈ 69.4 days: a new hop needs L_{k+1} > tip (receiver.rs:665) and invalidation_model.rs's own wall_clock_vs_hop_budget pins horizon_days(capacity) = 0. The honest cell is '0 vB/yr, at the price of exit-only after ~69 days — or ~589 vB/coin-yr to stay spendable'. Publishing the first clause alone reproduces the same defect at a finer grain. (2) T-2's SEVERITY LINE UNDERSTATES ITSELF, checkably: 'no user loses funds; what is lost is the document's authority'. The cadence is not merely uncounted, it is unpaid by default for idle received coins. auto_refresh_before_spend (transfer.rs:352,742) pays it only when the owner transacts; background_auto_refresh is false on both presets; and auto_exit_due never sees a whole coin at all, because estimate_exit_cost returns exit_deadline_block = None with no branch rows (wallet.rs:3118) and the pass skips it as 'verified flat: no ancestor can race it' (wallet.rs:1985). The parent is already terminal when the payee refuses, and both children are already minted; the sender recovers by broadcasting the retained flat backup over F — 112 vB, available almost at once because the refusal only fires near L_k — which voids the tree including the piece the payee declined. The alternative is the ladder walk at 293·d + 375 vB. Ceiling: one parent coin and one on-chain exit per occurrence, bounded above by the parent's own value.

Client verification is chain-anchored and fail-closed (utils.rs:143-200) and stores nothing. No high-water mark exists anywhere: high.water / last_attested / highest.attested return zero hits over clients/libs, and no coin record persists num_sigs. rejects_undercount (tesr.rs:13793-13796) is a three-line unit test asserting verify_bundle errors on an undercount — a predicate, not persisted state, exactly as the item says.

The rotation is loud only to a party who RUNS validate_tx0_output_pubkey, i.e. a receiver at claim. The current owner already claimed and never re-runs it; they would notice only on their next transfer. So a restore that DID span a transfer is still silent to the current owner for as long as they hold the coin, and the exposure window is 'until someone next claims or transfers', not 'until the restore completes'.

SHARPENING WHICH STORE MATTERS: the ATTESTED count the client verifies comes from the lockbox's own db_manager (server.cpp:471), while the coordinator's independent gate (sign.rs:106-116, :283-301) reads Postgres. A LOCKBOX-ONLY restore therefore cannot enable NEW co-signatures — the coordinator's gate still refuses them — but it fully HIDES existing ones, and hiding is the theft-enabler: a receiver's census balances while k rival states remain live. So the item's WHO/WHAT is right, and the single-store restore is sufficient; the two-store requirement applies only to the INV-19 fork variant. That distinction makes the cheap fix even more obviously free: the two stores already disagree in exactly the case that matters, and nothing reads the disagreement.

The item's framing correction is the right one and must survive into the spec: on the shipping deployment the lockbox is a plain C++ process with no SGX separation, so 'the host builds the digest' is not a boundary crossing — the OPERATOR'S STORAGE is the boundary.
items.exposure_if_open: WHO: the owner of any coin whose statechain id received co-signatures inside a restored window — and, for a transfer-spanning restore, still the owner, for as long as no party re-runs validate_tx0_output_pubkey. WHAT: up to 100% of the coin's value — the census's right-hand side under-reports, so k co-signed rival states stay hidden while exact-equality still balances, and a rival can then race the owner's state. WHEN: after any operator storage restore or failover of the LOCKBOX ALONE — a routine operations action, not an attack, which is what makes this worse than an adversary-gated hole: a well-meaning DBA can trigger it and nothing in the protocol, the docs or the runbooks says they must not. No document states durability or anti-rollback as a requirement; A3 states monotonicity as observed behaviour. The residual has no bound because nobody has computed how many co-signatures a restore can hide — the number is chosen by whoever performs the restore.

The seed is host-held (see exposure), the lockbox is plain C++ with no enclave boundary (D22), and SPEC-FOUNDATION §1 names the coordinator, the SSP and the blind SE as ONE operator trust domain. The privilege is UNCHANGED: process access to the operator's own stack. D8(a)'s real reduction should be stated as what it is and no more — it defeats a coordinator that does NOT hold the lockbox seed, i.e. a partial compromise (API server / Postgres popped, lockbox host intact) and any future deployment that separates the two. That is worth something; it is not the boundary the current text implies.

THIS STRENGTHENS THE ITEM'S OWN CONCLUSION AND KILLS THE 'BOUNDED-UNDER-B1' ESCAPE MORE CLEANLY THAN THE ITEM DOES. The attestation's authority reduces exactly to T-SE-1, not to a separate storage assumption. And the collusion sets are NOT equivalent in strength: B1's precondition is an ASSUMPTION VIOLATION (the SE retained a share it promised to erase, unverifiable from outside), while this one is ROUTINE OPERATIONAL ACCESS to a process the operator runs. Filing it under B1 would launder a normal capability as an exotic one.

ADD THE FAIL-CLOSED VARIANT. An accidental rollback (point-in-time restore after an outage) is the LIKELY event and it is a liveness disaster, not a theft — clients refuse the undercount. Naming both directions is what makes the row read as analysis rather than advocacy.

KEEP VERBATIM: the client half genuinely is closed and fail-closed (utils.rs:135-200 — refuses an unattested count outright, refuses a half-stated or absent budget rather than defaulting, carries a 32-byte caller nonce, verifies against enclave_public_key rather than the served attestation_pubkey); sealing does NOT close it for the reason given; and D8 option (c) — the append-only hash chain h_n = H(h_{n−1} ‖ sid ‖ n) published as a v3 digest field, one column and one hash per co-sign, no SGX — is the buildable half. The spec must state the assumption beside T-SE-1 explicitly; until it does, open is the honest bucket. owner_call = true stands: the bucket itself is the judgement.

items.residual: F10 / flaw RGB-2 — the coloured lane's economic security is denominated in carrier sats while the loss is denominated in asset value, and the plain flat backup is a BURN rather than a transfer
items.exposure_if_open: WHO: any payee holding a coloured allocation whose carrier sits below the sats cost of defending it at the prevailing rate. WHAT: the ENTIRE asset, and not to an attacker — to nobody. The allocation is closed by an RGB-unaware witness and DESTROYED; on the plain lane the voided piece's sats are recovered by the sender (so G8's attacker-gain bound genuinely holds there), and on the coloured lane nobody acquires what the payee loses, so no attacker-gain bound describes the victim's exposure at all. WHEN: the moment ANY prior owner of an ancestor broadcasts their retained 112-vB flat rung over F — ~224 sat at 2 sat/vB, voiding the tree in ONE transaction with ZERO marginal cost per additional piece, needing no malice. THE NUMBERS, STATED PER LANE (this is the fix): a coloured piece is carved at TOKEN_PIECE_SATS = 3,066 sat regardless of the asset value it carries. On the CTES-R coloured LADDERED lane — which is built but default-OFF (SdkConfig::colored_ladder = false, config.rs:357/:388, commit 2c351c6) and gated behind CR-D/D30 — defending it costs V_min shifted +172 for colour: ~70,016 sat at depth 1 / 50 sat/vB (23× the carrier), rising to ~329,072 at depth 10 / 50 (107×). On the SHIPPED un-laddered carrier lane (PROTOCOL.md:31 — 'an RGB carrier is deliberately never laddered') the defence is the signed-once branch, not a 3 + 2d walk, and the corresponding figure must be computed and published rather than inherited from the ladder table. WHY UNBOUNDED EITHER WAY: the loss is the asset's value, on which the design places no bound — every floor in the tree (min_child_value, colored_child_floor at tesr.rs:3372, colored_spine_tip_floor at :3383, V_min) is pure fee arithmetic with no asset term.
items.challenge:
THE CORE CLAIM STANDS, IS UNMITIGATED, AND APPEARS NOWHERE — but the headline ratio mixes two lanes that do not coexist on the shipped configuration, and that is the one number a reviewer will check first.

CONFIRMED: TOKEN_PIECE_SATS = 3,066 (tokens.rs:105, the coloured root floor at 2× head-room, independent of the asset carried); colored_child_floor and colored_spine_tip_floor are pure fee arithmetic; SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY states the 112-vB-versus-walk asymmetry, the 6×–265× range, the zero marginal cost and 'It needs no malice'. The one sentence that exists nowhere is the item's: on the coloured lane an allocation's security is denominated in its carrier's SATS and in the sats cost of defending that carrier, not in the asset's value. SUBECONOMIC-FINALITY:126's 'Colour is irrelevant to this finding' is true of the arithmetic and load-bearing-and-misleading about the consequence — the item is right to make that the amendment.

THE DEFECT: '3,066 sat … defending it at the enforced depth cap of 10 during a 50 sat/vB spike costs V_min = 328,900 — 107× the carrier's own sats' pairs a coloured-CARRIER mint floor with a LADDERED depth-10 SPLIT PIECE's defence cost. Those do not coexist today: colored_ladder defaults to FALSE and PROTOCOL.md:31 says a carrier is deliberately never laddered, so a shipped coloured piece's exit is the signed-once branch and V_min(10, 50) does not describe it. Two further slips in the same sentence: the coloured V_min is the plain table shifted +172 (SUBECONOMIC:126), so the figure is 329,072; and 'essentially every coloured piece at any realistic spike' is asserted rather than computed, when the per-lane numbers are available and are still damning (≈23× at depth 1 / 50 sat/vB).

RESTATED PER LANE THE ITEM IS STRONGER, NOT WEAKER: the exposure is present-tense on the un-laddered carrier lane at the branch cost, and becomes the V_min curve the moment D30/CR-D flips colored_ladder true — which is exactly the flip D32 was written to inventory. Label every number with its lane, or a reviewer who checks one constant against one default finds a cross-lane comparison and discards the row.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE ITEM IS CORRECT AND SHOULD BE KEPT VERBATIM: the three self-corrections (the sender's own change allocation rides the same tree so the worked scenario only holds where the sender retains none; abandonment alone destroys nothing — destruction requires a prior owner to actually spend F; and the remedy is CR-D plus DISCLOSURE, not refusal, with 'colour every retained rung' struck as RGB-1's attack generalised). items.residual: B5 — Onboarding window: the first backup (tx1) is co-signed only when the SE first SEES the funding tx
items.challenge: The bucket stands; the printed bound does not, and it contradicts another item in the same document. (1) ARITHMETIC IS WRONG. 'tx1's nLockTime is h_deposit + initlock − rand(0..99)' is false. The rand(0..=99) subtraction lives in get_locktime_for_withdrawal_transaction (lib/src/transaction.rs:94-107), reachable only when is_withdrawal == true, and even then only 1 time in 11 (rng.gen_range(0..=10) == 0). create_tx1 calls new_transaction(..., qt_backup_tx = 0, is_withdrawal = false, block_height = None, ...) (clients/libs/rust/src/deposit.rs:58-68), so calculate_block_height returns tip + initlock EXACTLY: L_0 = h + 10 000, no randomisation. The magnitude (10 000 blocks, 69.4 d) is right; the formula beside it is not, and it disagrees with T-1's own L_k = h_dep + initlock − interval·k in the same list (which at k=1 gives 9 900). A reviewer checks one formula, finds two versions, and stops reading. (2) THE STANDING EXPOSURE IS PROCEDURE, NOT A BOUND. The item itself argues the stated mitigation is 'user procedure, and procedure is not a mechanism' — then derives 'exactly ONE in-flight deposit' from that same unenforced procedure. It is a bound conditional on discipline the code does not enforce, and the owner does not always control funding timing (an inbound payment from a third party to the deposit address). Honest form: unbounded in COUNT, bounded per deposit at its own value, reducible to one by a procedure nothing checks. (3) A SECOND PARTY TO THE WINDOW IS UNNAMED. create_tx1 fires on the INITIALISED→IN_MEMPOOL transition, and that transition happens only when THIS wallet polls (clients/libs/rust/src/coin_status.rs:60-88). An owner who broadcasts funding and then goes offline holds the window open indefinitely with a live SE; no pass closes it. The window is bounded by min(SE liveness, OWNER liveness), not by SE liveness alone. (4) 'Nothing in the deposit path expires' is true only for epoch_deadline = NULL. Coins opened via get_deposit_bitcoin_address_single_use_epoch (clients/libs/rust/src/deposit.rs:19) carry an epoch_deadline that BOTH sign/first (server/src/endpoints/sign.rs:124-128) and sign/second (:303-318) enforce with a hard 410. For those, an SE outage spanning the deadline is permanent even after the SE returns — the sentence needs scoping.
items.the_bound: CORRECTED: per-deposit loss = the value of a deposit broadcast but not yet tx1-co-signed, under permanent SE loss OR permanent owner-side non-polling; unbounded in the NUMBER of such deposits, since nothing serialises funding. Once tx1 exists, tx1.nLockTime = h_funding_seen + initlock exactly (mainnet 10 000 blocks ≈ 69.4 days; regtest 1 000), with no randomisation — the rand term is withdrawal-only. Scope the 'nothing expires' clause to epoch_deadline = NULL coins.

items.residual: B10 — Split/combine commit ordering: the parent's spend budget is set terminal BEFORE child signatures and backups are durably persisted
items.challenge: Both named mechanisms check out — journal_write precedes set_spend_budget at EVERY terminalization site, not just the two cited (tesr.rs:2779→2781, 4071→4074, 5766→5768, 6327→6329, 7693 preceded by :7690), and the lockbox cache sits ahead of BOTH the secnonce consume and the D8(i) budget check (lockbox/src/server.cpp:105-135). The bucket stands. Two corrections to the bound. (a) 'A window one HTTP round-trip long' understates it and mis-names what it covers. The window is one round trip PLUS cosign_tier's whole in-process retry budget (5 attempts, ~3 s of backoff, tesr.rs:13865-13884), and the cache rescues only a retry that re-sends the IDENTICAL session. Nothing journals the signing session: the Planned record carries the unsigned tier (PendingTier{txid, tx_hex, prev_value, out_value, csv, payload_vout}), never partial.encoded_session / client_partial_sig. So a PROCESS DEATH inside the window necessarily mints a new session on restart — the case cosign_tier's own comment calls unrecoverable — and the write-ahead journal does not cover it. The mitigation is 'in-process transport loss', not 'crash'; saying 'everything except one signature is replayable' overstates it. (b) THE TWO COUNTERS ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS AND THE BOUND TREATS THEM AS ONE. The 410 gate reads the COORDINATOR's count_finalized_signatures over statechain_signature_data (server/src/database/deposit.rs:156-163); the receiver census reads the ENCLAVE's attested sig_count (server/src/endpoints/transfer_receiver.rs:95). They diverge whenever set_partial_sig_issued fails AFTER a successful enclave co-sign — sign.rs:417-424 returns 500 'retry' with the enclave's count already advanced. The budget gate then does not arm, every fresh-session retry burns another enclave slot, and 'exactly ONE co-signature per split' fails. On a coin with no budget the enclave's own D8(i) cap does not apply either, so nothing caps it.
items.the_bound: CORRECTED: one co-signature per split under in-process transport loss (the budget-exhausting SP), window = one HTTP round trip plus ~3 s of cosign_tier retries; one further co-signature per PROCESS DEATH inside that window, which the journal does not cover because the signing session is never journalled; and UNBOUNDED under a coordinator DB fault that lets the enclave's sig_count run ahead of count_finalized_signatures. Damage class unchanged and correct: cooperative path only, value exits on the parent's pre-signed chain, state recorded as SplitStage::Stranded (tesr.rs:4318-4322).

A patched sender declares protocol_version = 3; the claim path skips the >= 4 recipient binding (:1227), takes the legacy branch (:1598), adopts exit-only and books CONFIRMED at the SP output's value, while the sender retains the child's auth key and un-rotated SE share AND the child carries no spend budget at all — so the number of rival tiers the sender can co-sign is unbounded, not one. items.residual: gap_an_ancestor_split_state_may_mint_value_out_of_nothing — plus: the COMBINE lane was never swept

items.residual: R-2 — No unconditional no-watch window: a received coin must be watched from the moment of receipt, forever
items.challenge: Every number checks out against lib/src/tesr.rs:256 (d0 1440, δ 36, d_floor 144, e0 720, δE 36, e_floor 144, m_max 15, rate 2.0), :375-386, and 2 160/144 = 15.0 days. D14 is confirmed unimplemented ('Implementation is WP3c', DECISIONS.md:174) and D31 is correctly carried. THE BOUND IS STILL WRONG, AND IT IS WRONG BY CONTRADICTING ANOTHER ITEM IN THE SAME LIST. R-2 asserts 'nothing ages while the coin is un-triggered' and concludes 'the obligation is be reachable inside 24 h, not act daily'. T-1, four items later, establishes the opposite for the ordinary case: a RECEIVED whole laddered coin RETAINS the absolute flat-backup ladder, so a prior owner's rung L_{k−1} = h_deposit + 10 000 − 100(k−1) becomes spendable at a fixed calendar height, spends F directly in one 112-vB transaction and voids the entire tree — with NO trigger broadcast and nothing to react to. The honest holder's head start there is interval = 100 blocks (~16.7 h), which is SHORTER than the 24 h R-2 quotes as its floor, and it runs unconditionally. TRUST-MODEL.md's B4 row carries the identical false claim ('On the laddered shape there is no calendar deadline at all'). Two named limitations that refute each other is the single most quotable defect a reviewer can find in a soundness document; whichever of the two is right, the other discredits it. Second, smaller, and checkable with a calculator: 'only a fully-renewed coin sits at the 144-block floor' is true of the STATE tier (needs_renewal(k) first fires at k = 36, and state_csv(36) = 1440 − 1296 = 144 exactly) but NOT of the extension tier — needs_rollover(m) fires at m ≥ 15 and ext_csv(15) = 720 − 540 = 180, so e_floor = 144 is a clamp the schedule never reaches. 'At least 144' remains a valid conservative lower bound, so this is a precision defect, not a safety one; state it as ≥ 180 in operation, floored at 144.
items.the_bound: CORRECTED, two clocks not one. (1) REACTIVE clock, as stated and verified: after a hostile T confirms, ≥ e_floor = 144 blocks (≥ 180 in practice) before any rival can spend T.out[0], and ≥ d_floor = 144 more before a rival state confirms; a fresh coin has 720 + 1440 = 2 160 blocks ≈ 15 days; missing it costs the entire coin. (2) ABSOLUTE clock, omitted and load-bearing: a received coin carrying a flat ladder must produce ONE confirmed spend of F before L_{k−1} = h_deposit + 10 000 − 100(k−1), with only interval = 100 blocks (~16.7 h) of head start over the prior owner, running whether or not anything is triggered. The obligation is therefore 'be reachable inside ~16.7 h AND act before a fixed calendar height', not 'be reachable inside 24 h'. Delete 'nothing ages while the coin is un-triggered' here and in TRUST-MODEL B4, or retract T-1.

items.residual: SPINE / TRUC residuals — a third party can occupy an unconfirmed spine tier's single TRUC child slot for 240 sat
items.challenge: Bucket stands — the squat contest is genuinely uncomputed and the sequencing numbers verify (max_exit_txs mainnet 23 at depth 10, regtest 139, depth-1 walk 2 885 blocks of a 10 000-block epoch, lib/src/transfer/receiver.rs:899-955; SPINE_CSV = 0 at tesr.rs:6803; P2A_VALUE = 240 and committed_fee_rate 2.0 at lib/src/tesr.rs:41,:256). items.challenge: The item's best work survives: the SE genuinely never sees a sighash (PartialSignatureRequestPayload = {statechain_id, negate_seckey, session, signed_statechain_id, server_pub_nonce}, lib/src/transaction.rs:44-50), so the finding's proposed sighash register is correctly refused; the lockbox cache is real and correctly ordered (lockbox/src/server.cpp:105-135, ahead of both the secnonce consume and D8(i)); the coordinator's 410 does sit in front of it (sign.rs:293-299 vs the lockbox POST at :242+); the ancestor census re-run is at tesr.rs:11953-11958. The bound says the loss is confined to 'the co-signature that EXHAUSTS the budget: every other lost reply is served identically from the enclave's session-keyed cache on retry.' That holds only where the client re-sends the SAME session, and exactly ONE entry point does — cosign_tier (tesr.rs:13850-13884, whose comment says so). The un-laddered lane does not, on three counts at once: (a) mercuryrustlib::transaction::new_transaction calls sign_second once and propagates the error (clients/libs/rust/src/transaction.rs:53) with no retry loop, and the session lives only in coin.secret_nonce / server_public_nonce, which the next attempt overwrites via create_and_commit_nonces — so the retry is a NEW session the cache cannot serve; (b) plain coins carry NO spend budget at all (set_spend_budget is only ever called with remaining: 1 and only on split parents/tips: tesr.rs:2781, 4074, 5768, 6329, 7693), so the 410 never fires and there is no budget-exhausting signature to confine the loss to; (c) the census on that lane is hard equality — `statechain_info.num_sigs != transfer_msg.backup_transactions.len()` ⇒ 'num_sigs is not correct' (transfer_receiver.rs:1482) — and INV-5's exact-decrement rule blocks padding the backup vector to rebalance. The damage CLASS the item states survives intact (cooperative path only; value exits unilaterally; sub-economic finality is the real floor). Only the bound is wrong — and a bound that is wrong on the majority lane is worse than admitting the exposure. This returns to bounded-accepted the moment the bound is restated AND the same-session re-serve is made normative on every lane; the mechanism already exists in the lockbox and only cosign_tier uses it.

Unbounded in count on budgetless coins, and unbounded under a coordinator DB fault that lets the enclave's sig_count run ahead of count_finalized_signatures. Damage confined to the cooperative path; the pre-signed chain is intact and the value exits unilaterally, which is a real bound only while the coin's value exceeds its exit cost at the exit-time fee rate. Reporting gap is worse than stated: SplitStage::Stranded exists on the split lane only, and the flat lane has no journal at all.
items.exposure_if_open: The owner of any un-laddered coin — every deposit and every flat transfer — loses the cooperative path permanently on a single lost sign/second response, because the retry mints a fresh session the enclave cache cannot serve, num_sigs overshoots backup_transactions.len() forever, and the receiver's exact-equality check refuses the coin at transfer_receiver.rs:1482 with no path back (padding is blocked by INV-5).
